stories.category: World — International Law and Human Rights
stories.headline: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar responsible for genocide against Rohingya
stories.summary: On 19 November, the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar's 2017 military campaign against the Rohingya amounted to genocide, in a case brought by The Gambia.
stories.what_happened: Reuters reported the UN's principal judicial organ found killings and widespread sexual violence met the genocide threshold. The case was filed by The Gambia in 2019. The judgment concerns state responsibility under international law, not individual criminal convictions.
stories.background: The Rohingya are a persecuted minority in Myanmar. The ICJ hears disputes between states, whereas the International Criminal Court prosecutes individuals.
stories.why_it_matters: The ruling is a major development in the interpretation and enforcement of the Genocide Convention and accountability for mass atrocities.
stories.pakistan_perspective: The judgment is relevant to Pakistan's positions on human rights, refugee protection and international legal remedies.
quick_gk: The Gambia brought the ICJ genocide case against Myanmar concerning the Rohingya.
question_angles: Which country instituted the Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar at the ICJ?

sources.title: Top UN court finds Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against Muslim Rohingya

stories.headline: Pakistan and Qatar sign internal-security cooperation memorandum
stories.summary: Pakistan and Qatar signed a memorandum of understanding on security cooperation and an action plan against drug smuggling on 19 November.
stories.what_happened: According to Pakistan's Prime Minister's Office as reported by Dawn, the memorandum links Qatar's Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya) and Pakistan's Federal Constabulary. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Qatari counterpart Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani signed the documents in the presence of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
stories.background: Pakistan and Qatar maintain ties in energy, migration and regional diplomacy. The latest instrument concerns internal security rather than a new defence alliance.
stories.why_it_matters: Institutional cooperation can facilitate information exchange and operational coordination against transnational smuggling.
stories.pakistan_perspective: The action plan addresses cross-border narcotics trafficking, while bilateral relations also include LNG supply and Pakistani workers in Qatar.
quick_gk: Pakistan and Qatar signed a security MoU between the Federal Constabulary and Qatar's Lekhwiya on 19 November 2026.
question_angles: Which Pakistani force was named in the 19 November Pakistan–Qatar security memorandum?

sources.title: Pakistan, Qatar sign MoU on security cooperation

stories.headline: Xi warns Trump over Taiwan during Shenzhen APEC diplomacy
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping told US President Donald Trump that Washington should handle Taiwan carefully, according to a 19 November Chinese state-media account of their talks.
stories.what_happened: Reuters reported Xinhua's description of the Xi–Trump meeting as positive and constructive, with an intention to develop an action plan for a strategically stable relationship. The readout offered no detailed settlement on Taiwan or US arms sales.
stories.background: Taiwan participates in APEC as Chinese Taipei, while Beijing regards the island as part of China and Taipei rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims.
stories.why_it_matters: Taiwan remains a central flashpoint in US–China relations and the security of semiconductor supply chains.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Stability in East Asia matters for Pakistan's technology imports and trade, while Islamabad maintains a one-China policy.
quick_gk: Xi Jinping and Donald Trump held talks in Shenzhen during APEC diplomacy on 19 November 2026.
question_angles: Which Chinese city hosted Xi–Trump talks on 19 November 2026?

sources.title: China's Xi says US should do 'right thing' on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in relations

stories.headline: Revised COP31 draft drops fossil-fuel language and specific adaptation-finance target
stories.summary: COP31 negotiators circulated a revised draft on 19 November that omitted references to fossil fuels and an earlier proposed $120 billion adaptation-finance benchmark.
stories.what_happened: Reuters reported the revised Antalya text removed the fossil-fuel language and the specific finance target while retaining calls for deep emissions cuts. It was a negotiating draft, not an adopted final agreement.
stories.background: COP decisions require negotiations among parties with differing responsibilities, energy systems and financing priorities.
stories.why_it_matters: The revisions show the difficulty of reconciling mitigation commitments and financial support for vulnerable countries.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan has a strong interest in predictable adaptation finance and climate-resilient infrastructure.
quick_gk: The 19 November COP31 revised draft removed an earlier proposed $120 billion adaptation-finance target.
question_angles: Which proposed annual adaptation-finance benchmark was omitted from the revised COP31 draft on 19 November?

sources.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels

stories.headline: El Niño risks compound developing-country adaptation funding shortfall
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 19 November that strong El Niño conditions were amplifying food-security risks as COP31 negotiators debated adaptation finance.
stories.what_happened: The report cited estimates that developing countries require around $300 billion annually for adaptation but received approximately $36 billion in 2024, while the current El Niño threatens agriculture in several regions.
stories.background: El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation and alters rainfall and temperature patterns around the world.
stories.why_it_matters: Climate shocks can reduce crop yields, disrupt fisheries and strain already limited adaptation resources.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan's agriculture and water security are exposed to climate variability, making early-warning systems and adaptation funding relevant.
quick_gk: Reuters reported on 19 November 2026 that developing countries need about $300 billion annually for climate adaptation.
question_angles: What annual adaptation-finance requirement for developing countries was cited in Reuters' 19 November COP31 report?

sources.title: El Nino raises the stakes as COP31 wrestles over finance
